description: Comprehensive E2E Testing Framework - Systematic quality improvement through factor analysis, 3-way combinatorial test matrix, and rigorous end-to-end testing covering all modes, key bindings, boundary conditions, and invalid inputs

userStories.title: Factor analysis table
userStories.description: As a developer, I want a structured table enumerating all testable factors so that I can reason about coverage systematically.
acceptanceCriteria: Create tasks/e2e-factor-analysis.md containing a factor table
Factors organized by category: Editor Mode, Cursor Position, Buffer State, Key Input, File State, Terminal Dimensions, Window Configuration
Each factor lists all possible levels (values) — e.g., Mode = {Normal, Search Forward, Search Backward, Minibuffer, Confirm, C-x Prefix, Grep}
Include 'no-op / irrelevant key' as an explicit factor level for Key Input
Each factor assigned a priority: Critical (must test), Important (should test), Edge-case (nice to have)
Cover at least 15 factors with 3-7 levels each
Document rationale for priority assignments
Typecheck passes (go vet ./...)
userStories.notes: Read main.go, buffer.go, command.go, grep.go to enumerate ALL key bindings, modes, and buffer states. Include factors for: editor mode (7 levels), cursor row position (4 levels), cursor column position (4 levels), buffer content type (6 levels), modification state (2 levels), mark state (3 levels), kill ring state (2 levels), undo stack state (3 levels), read-only flag (2 levels), key class (7 levels), file backing (3 levels), highlighter state (2 levels), window count (3 levels), active window (2 levels), terminal size (3 levels).

userStories.title: No-op and boundary condition test case definitions
userStories.description: As a developer, I want explicit test case definitions for no-op keys and boundary conditions so that edge cases are systematically covered.
acceptanceCriteria: Create tasks/e2e-noop-boundary-cases.md with structured test case tables

Define no-op test cases for each editor mode: Normal (unbound keys like C-q, C-o), Search (C-x, C-v), Minibuffer (C-n, C-p, C-v), Confirm (any key except y/n/C-g), C-x Prefix (invalid second keys like C-x a, C-x z), Grep (unbound keys like x, C-f)
At least 30 no-op/invalid input test cases across all modes

Define boundary condition test cases: empty buffer (backspace, delete, kill, movement at boundaries), single character buffer (delete then undo), large content (1000+ lines, 500+ char line), undo stack limit (101 edits, 100 undos), consecutive kill accumulation (50+ C-k), minimum window size (2-3 rows after splits)
Each test case has: ID (TC-NOOP-NNN or TC-BOUND-NNN), precondition, input sequence, expected post-condition
Typecheck passes (go vet ./...)
userStories.notes: This is a design document, not code. Focus on being exhaustive for no-op keys — every mode should have at least 5 no-op test cases defined. For boundary conditions, focus on the extremes: empty buffers, maximum undo stack (100 entries, maxUndoEntries constant in buffer.go), and minimum window sizes.

userStories.title: Test matrix design with 3-way combinatorial coverage
userStories.description: As a developer, I want a combinatorial test matrix that covers 3-way factor interactions so that I can achieve high coverage without combinatorial explosion.
acceptanceCriteria: Create tasks/e2e-test-matrix.md containing the test matrix
Use 3-way (t=3) combinatorial coverage: every combination of any 3 factor levels appears in at least one test case
Each row defines: Test Case ID, factor values, input sequence, expected post-condition (cursor position, buffer content, mode, message line)
Group test cases by theme: Movement, Editing, Kill/Yank, Search, Buffer Management, Window Management, Grep Mode, Minibuffer, Error Handling / No-ops
Document excluded combinations with rationale (e.g., Grep mode + Confirm mode cannot coexist)
Target: 200-400 test cases total
Each test case has unique ID in format TC-{group}-{number} (e.g., TC-MOV-001, TC-EDIT-015)
Typecheck passes (go vet ./...)
userStories.notes: Reference tasks/e2e-factor-analysis.md for factors and tasks/e2e-noop-boundary-cases.md for edge cases. Infeasible combinations to prune: Grep mode + Confirm mode, Read-only buffer + Editing operation (tested separately in no-op), Minibuffer mode + Window commands, Search mode + C-x prefix. Consider using a covering array algorithm or manual construction. Group by theme for readability.

userStories.title: Failure log infrastructure
userStories.description: As a developer, I want test failures recorded in a machine-parseable JSON log so that I can triage issues efficiently.
acceptanceCriteria: Create e2e/failure_logger.go with a RecordFailure function
RecordFailure signature: RecordFailure(t *testing.T, caseID string, input string, expected string, actual string, severity string, category string)
Writes failure records to tasks/e2e-failures.json as a JSON array
Each record contains: test_case_id, test_name, input_sequence, expected_state, actual_state, severity, category, timestamp (RFC3339)
Severity levels: critical (crash/data loss), high (wrong behavior), medium (cosmetic), low (minor)
Log is append-only during test run; a ResetFailureLog() function clears the file at start of suite
Use sync.Mutex for thread-safe writes
Output file is valid JSON (array of objects)
go vet ./e2e/... passes
Typecheck passes (go vet ./...)
userStories.notes: The failure logger is a helper used by all comprehensive test files. It should read the existing file on first write (if any), append the new record, and write back. Use encoding/json with MarshalIndent for readable output. The file path should be relative to the project root — use a package-level var or detect it from the test binary location.

userStories.title: Comprehensive movement tests
userStories.description: As a developer, I want automated E2E tests for all cursor movement operations across various buffer states.
acceptanceCriteria: Create e2e/comprehensive_movement_test.go with TestComprehensiveMovement test group
Test all movement keys: C-f, C-b, C-n, C-p, C-a, C-e, C-v, M-v, M-<, M->
Test arrow keys: Left, Right, Up, Down
Test each movement at boundary positions (start of buffer, end of buffer, start of line, end of line)
Test C-f at end of line wraps to next line
Test C-b at start of line wraps to previous line
Test C-n/C-p with column clamping (moving from long line to short line)

All tests pass
go vet ./e2e/... passes
Typecheck passes (go vet ./...)
userStories.notes: Use existing Harness from harness.go. Create temp files with known content for multi-line tests. Use AssertCursorAt() to verify cursor positions after each movement. For page up/down boundary tests, create a file with exactly 30 lines and test C-v at line 20 (less than a full page remaining). For column clamping, create lines of different lengths (e.g., 'short' and 'this is a longer line') and verify cursor column after C-n/C-p.

userStories.title: Comprehensive editing tests
userStories.description: As a developer, I want automated E2E tests for all text editing operations including edge cases.
acceptanceCriteria: Create e2e/comprehensive_editing_test.go with TestComprehensiveEditing test group
Test InsertChar with ASCII, multi-byte UTF-8 characters
Test tab character insertion and visual expansion (tab at column 0 shows 8 spaces, tab at column 3 shows 5 spaces)
Test Backspace: middle of line, start of line (join with previous), in empty buffer (no change)
Test C-d: middle of line, end of line (join with next), in empty buffer (no change)
Test Enter/C-j: middle of line (split), end of line, start of line

userStories.notes: For UTF-8 test, insert a multibyte character like a Japanese character and verify it appears in screen capture. For tab expansion, insert a tab and use screen capture to count the visual spaces. For read-only buffer test, open a file, then create a *Buffer List* buffer (C-x C-b) which is read-only, and try editing in it.

userStories.title: Comprehensive kill, yank, and region tests
userStories.description: As a developer, I want automated E2E tests for kill ring, yank, and region operations.
acceptanceCriteria: Create e2e/comprehensive_killyank_test.go with TestComprehensiveKillYank test group
Test C-k at end of line (joins next line), on empty line, consecutive kills accumulate in kill ring
Test C-k then non-kill key (C-f) then C-k: verify kill ring entries are separate (second yank gets second kill only)
Test C-w: single-line region, multi-line region, zero-width region (mark == point)
Test M-w: copies without deleting, verify subsequent C-y pastes correctly
Test C-y: single-line yank, multi-line yank, yank into empty buffer
Test C-y with empty kill ring: no change to buffer
Test region + yank interaction: set mark, move, kill region, move elsewhere, yank
All tests pass
go vet ./e2e/... passes
Typecheck passes (go vet ./...)
userStories.notes: For consecutive kill accumulation test: C-k twice on a two-line buffer, then move and C-y — should paste both killed lines. For separate kills test: C-k, then C-f (breaks consecutive chain), then C-k, then C-y — should only paste the second kill. For M-w (copy region), send C-Space to set mark, move with C-f/C-n, then Escape w to copy, then C-y to paste.

userStories.title: Comprehensive search tests
userStories.description: As a developer, I want automated E2E tests for incremental search in all edge cases.
acceptanceCriteria: Create e2e/comprehensive_search_test.go with TestComprehensiveSearch test group
Test search with no matches: 'Failing I-search' message shown
Test forward search wrap-around: search from near end wraps to beginning
Test backward search wrap-around: search from near beginning wraps to end
Test search cancel (C-g): cursor returns to original position
Test search accept (Enter): cursor stays at match
Test search exit via unrecognized key: key is re-processed in normal mode (e.g., C-a during search exits and moves to beginning of line)
Test search with empty query: no crash, handles gracefully
Test backspace in search query re-searches from original position
Test switching direction: C-s to start forward, then C-r to reverse within same search
All tests pass
go vet ./e2e/... passes
Typecheck passes (go vet ./...)
userStories.notes: For wrap-around test, create a file with 'target' on line 3 of 10. Move cursor to line 8, press C-s and type 'target' — should wrap and find it on line 3. For direction switch, press C-s to start forward search, type query, then press C-r to switch to backward. Verify cursor moves to the match before current position.

userStories.title: Comprehensive undo tests
userStories.description: As a developer, I want automated E2E tests for the undo system including limits.
acceptanceCriteria: Create e2e/comprehensive_undo_test.go with TestComprehensiveUndo test group
Test undo of character insertion: insert char, C-_ undo, verify char removed
Test undo of deletion: C-d delete char, undo, verify char restored
Test undo of kill line: C-k, undo, verify line restored
Test undo of region kill: set mark, move, C-w, undo, verify region restored
Test undo of yank: C-y, undo, verify yanked text removed
Test undo of newline insertion: Enter, undo, verify lines joined back
Test undo stack empty: undo with no changes, verify no crash
Test undo after save: undo is still available after C-x C-s
All tests pass
go vet ./e2e/... passes
Typecheck passes (go vet ./...)

For undo stack limit test (101 edits, 100 undos), this may be slow — consider testing with a smaller number first (e.g., 10 edits, 10 undos) to verify the mechanism, then a separate subtest for the limit.

userStories.title: Comprehensive buffer management tests
userStories.description: As a developer, I want automated E2E tests for multi-buffer operations and edge cases.
acceptanceCriteria: Create e2e/comprehensive_buffer_test.go with TestComprehensiveBuffer test group
Test C-x C-f with existing file: opens file, content shown, status bar shows filename
Test C-x C-f with nonexistent file: new empty buffer created with filename set
Test C-x C-f with same file already open: switches to existing buffer (no duplicate)
Test C-x b with default (previous buffer): verify switching works
Test C-x b with typed buffer name: verify correct buffer shown
Test C-x k on unmodified buffer: closes without confirmation
Test C-x k on modified buffer: y confirms close, n cancels close
Test C-x C-b: buffer list shows all open buffers with correct markers (> current, * modified)
Test C-x C-b then Enter: switches to selected buffer
All tests pass
go vet ./e2e/... passes
Typecheck passes (go vet ./...)
userStories.notes: For 'same file already open' test, open a file with C-x C-f, switch to scratch, then C-x C-f the same file again — verify no duplicate buffer in C-x C-b list. For kill modified buffer, type something first to make the buffer modified, then C-x k. For buffer list markers, the format is: '>' prefix for current buffer, '*' for modified.

userStories.title: Comprehensive window management tests
userStories.description: As a developer, I want automated E2E tests for window splitting, switching, and closing edge cases.
acceptanceCriteria: Create e2e/comprehensive_window_test.go with TestComprehensiveWindow test group
Test C-x 2: vertical split, both windows show same buffer, two status lines visible
Test C-x 3: horizontal split, both windows side-by-side, vertical separator drawn
Test C-x o: cycles through windows (verify active window changes via status line style)
Test C-x 0: closes current window, layout recalculates to single window
Test C-x 0 with only one window: verify no crash, appropriate message or no action
Test C-x 1: closes all other windows, only active window remains
Test editing in split windows: edit in one window, verify change visible in other window showing same buffer
Test independent scroll: scroll in window 0, verify window 1 scroll position unchanged
All tests pass
go vet ./e2e/... passes
Typecheck passes (go vet ./...)
userStories.notes: For testing status lines, use screen capture and check for '==' (active) vs '--' (inactive) markers. For independent scroll test, split window, scroll down in active window with C-v, switch to other window with C-x o, verify its content is still at the top. For edit propagation, type in one window, switch to other, verify the typed text appears.

userStories.title: Comprehensive minibuffer tests

Test minibuffer editing: C-d (delete forward), C-k (kill to end), Backspace (delete backward)
Test minibuffer cancel with C-g: clears input and returns to normal mode
Test minibuffer cancel with Esc: clears input and returns to normal mode
Test Tab completion for file paths: partial path completes to longest common prefix
Test Tab completion for M-x commands: partial command name completes

userStories.title: Comprehensive grep mode tests

userStories.title: Comprehensive comment/uncomment tests

Test comment-region on Go file: set mark, select lines, M-x comment-region — adds '// ' prefix to each line
Test uncomment-region on Go file: select commented lines, M-x uncomment-region — removes '// ' prefix

Test comment-region on Python file: adds '# ' prefix
Test uncomment-region tolerates leading whitespace before comment marker
Test comment then uncomment round-trip: content returns to original state

userStories.title: Comprehensive no-op and invalid input tests
userStories.description: As a developer, I want automated E2E tests that verify the editor handles unexpected/no-op key presses gracefully.
acceptanceCriteria: Create e2e/comprehensive_noop_test.go with TestComprehensiveNoop test group
Test C-x followed by invalid second key (C-x a, C-x z, C-x C-q): prefix cancelled, no crash, editor still functional
Test unbound control keys in normal mode (C-q, C-o, C-t): no crash, buffer unchanged or character inserted
Test rapid key repeat: send 100 C-f presses in quick succession — cursor stops at buffer end, no crash
Test rapid mode switching: C-s then immediately C-g repeated 20 times — no state corruption
Test C-g in every mode: Normal (deactivate mark), Search (cancel), Minibuffer (cancel), C-x prefix (cancel)
Test keys in confirm mode: any key except y/n/C-g does nothing, stays in confirm prompt
Verify buffer content and cursor position unchanged after every no-op sequence
All tests pass
go vet ./e2e/... passes
Typecheck passes (go vet ./...)
userStories.notes: For confirm mode test: modify a buffer, then C-x k to trigger 'Buffer modified; kill anyway? (y/n)' prompt. Press various invalid keys (a, C-f, Enter) and verify the prompt remains. For rapid mode switching, use a loop sending C-s then C-g with minimal sleep. After the loop, verify the buffer is unchanged by comparing screen capture. For C-x invalid key, send C-x then 'a' and verify the editor returns to normal mode.

userStories.title: Comprehensive terminal resize tests

Test resize from 80x24 to 40x12: editor redraws correctly, content still visible
Test resize from 80x24 to 200x50: editor expands, no rendering artifacts
Test resize with split windows (C-x 2): windows recalculate heights correctly after resize
Test resize during search mode: search state preserved, search query still shown
Test resize during minibuffer input: input text preserved after resize
All tests pass

Typecheck passes (go vet ./...)

For search mode resize, enter C-s and type a query, resize, then verify the message line still shows the search prompt with the query.

userStories.title: Comprehensive cross-feature interaction tests
userStories.description: As a developer, I want E2E tests that verify correct behavior when multiple features interact.
acceptanceCriteria: Create e2e/comprehensive_interaction_test.go with TestComprehensiveInteraction test group
Test search while region is active: enter search, verify mark behavior after search exit
Test undo after yank: C-y to paste, C-_ to undo, verify yanked text removed
Test undo after kill region: C-w to kill, C-_ to undo, verify region text restored
Test C-x C-f during search mode: exits search and opens find-file prompt
Test split window then kill buffer: C-x 2 split, C-x k kill buffer, window shows next buffer
Test comment-region then undo: M-x comment-region, C-_ undo, comments removed

All tests pass
go vet ./e2e/... passes
Typecheck passes (go vet ./...)
userStories.notes: These tests exercise the interaction between subsystems. For undo after yank: first kill a line (C-k), move somewhere, paste (C-y), then undo (C-_) — verify the pasted text disappears. For save then undo: type text, save, undo the text, verify [Modified] reappears in status bar. For search + find-file: press C-s, type query, then C-x C-f — search should exit and find-file prompt should appear.

userStories.title: Full test suite execution and failure report
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to execute the full comprehensive E2E test suite and generate a complete failure report.
acceptanceCriteria: All comprehensive test files compile with go build ./e2e/...
Run full suite with: go test ./e2e/ -v -run TestComprehensive -timeout 30m
Test execution completes without panics or hangs
tasks/e2e-failures.json is generated with all detected failures (if any)
Tests are deterministic: running twice produces the same pass/fail results
Tests are isolated: each test creates its own tmux session and temp files
Print summary: total tests, passed, failed by severity
Typecheck passes (go vet ./...)
userStories.notes: This story is about running the full suite and collecting results. If any tests fail, record them using the failure logger from US-004. Review the failures and categorize by severity. Do NOT fix bugs in this story — that is handled in subsequent stories. Focus on ensuring all tests run to completion and the failure report is generated.

userStories.title: Bug fixes — critical severity (crashes, data loss)
userStories.description: As a developer, I want all critical-severity bugs fixed so that the editor is stable.
acceptanceCriteria: Review all critical-severity entries in tasks/e2e-failures.json
Fix each critical bug in the goomacs source code (main.go, buffer.go, command.go, grep.go, or term/)
Re-run affected test cases to confirm fix
Zero critical-severity failures remain after fixes
No regressions: existing baseline E2E tests still pass (go test ./e2e/ -run 'Test[^C]')
Typecheck passes (go vet ./...)
userStories.notes: If tasks/e2e-failures.json has no critical entries, mark this story as passed immediately. Critical bugs include: editor crashes (panic), data loss (buffer content corrupted), hangs (infinite loop). Fix the root cause in the source code, not by adjusting the test.

userStories.title: Bug fixes — high severity (wrong behavior)
userStories.description: As a developer, I want all high-severity bugs fixed so that the editor behaves correctly.

Fix each high-severity bug in the goomacs source code
Re-run affected test cases to confirm fix
Zero high-severity failures remain after fixes

Typecheck passes (go vet ./...)
userStories.notes: If tasks/e2e-failures.json has no high-severity entries, mark this story as passed immediately. High-severity bugs include: wrong cursor position after operation, incorrect buffer content after edit, wrong mode state after transition, incorrect message displayed. Fix the root cause in the source code.

userStories.title: Bug fixes — medium and low severity
userStories.description: As a developer, I want medium and low-severity bugs assessed and fixed where practical.
